lines.trans: Before splicing this together, let me see the raw footage one more time.
Thank you for working so late. Here is some coffee, please go ahead.
Please make sure to get some rest whenever you can.
Someday I want to create a work like the ones you and Mr. Muranishi made.

words.gram: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing appearance or likeness.

lines.trans: You should film the kind of work that you yourself love.
I'll do my best. Ms. Kuroki, aren't you going to appear in videos anymore?
Perish the thought! I will still make plenty more works.
I'm so glad to hear that. I look forward to them.

words.gloss: something to look forward to; fun

lines.trans: Director, he was working remarkably hard in there.
I'm counting on him. Our future sales depend on those guys.
Everyone is spreading their wings so fast. I can't afford to fall behind.
You're soaring higher than anyone, Kuroki. Keep boosting us as our poster girl.

lines.trans: See you later.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: しかたないだろ！こんな状況ですぐに対応できるはずがない。
examples.trans: Give them a break! Nobody can adjust right away in a situation like this.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

examples.text: お疲れさまでございます。これコーヒーです、どうぞ。
examples.trans: Thank you for working so late. Here is some coffee, please go ahead.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

examples.text: 先に到着して、今はホテルで休んでますよ。
examples.trans: She arrived ahead of you and is resting at the hotel right now.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
頑張ります! is the classic cheerful commitment when starting a job or task.

examples.trans: I will do my best today too.
Do your best on the exam!

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Introduces a stunned guess ('don't tell me... / surely you aren't...').

examples.text: まさか来ないとは思いませんでした。
examples.trans: I never thought they wouldn't come.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。
頼りにしてるよ。これからの売り上げはあいつらにかかってるからな。
examples.trans: I'm counting on him. Our future sales depend on those guys.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for time.

examples.text: いつまでも待っています。

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Polite way to address a group of people.

examples.text: 皆さんにお知らせがあります。
examples.trans: I have an announcement for everyone.

examples.text: まだ羽があるなら、ほら、逃げてみろよ。空へ飛んでけ！
examples.trans: If you've still got wings, go on, try escaping. Fly off into the sky!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: アニメの知識なら誰にも負けません。
examples.trans: When it comes to anime knowledge, I won't lose to anyone.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 黒木君が一番羽ばたいてるじゃないか。これからも広告塔としてもり立ててくれ。
examples.trans: You're soaring higher than anyone, Kuroki. Keep boosting us as our poster girl.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
